title: TrustLens Input Envelope
description: Phase 2 WP2. The canonical, versioned boundary between RAW TrustLens input and the deterministic detection knowledge layer. An envelope carries the submitted artefact plus whatever channel/parser metadata is available; it is NOT a detection and carries NO verdict, score or indicator. Downstream the normaliser turns an envelope into typed observations (observation.schema.json), which the indicator layer turns into indicator observations (indicator-observation.schema.json), which the existing rule engine consumes. This schema fixes the SHAPE only; referential integrity, ID resolution and the ban on a verdict leaking in are enforced by knowledge/validation/validate_extraction.py. Storage is deliberately unspecified (ADR-0004). Language/script are carried as data and MUST NOT be assumed English-only, so that resolving OI-04 / ADR-0014 is a data change, not a schema migration. Data minimisation (NFR/DPDP): a field being expressible here is not licence to populate it — see privacy.redaction.

envelope_version.description: Version of THIS envelope contract the instance was produced against. Const per contract revision (KB-001 §8: a bump is a governed change, not silent).

input_id.description: Opaque, stable identifier for this submission. Not derived from content; not a hash of PII.

input_type.description: The modality of the submission. Not all modalities are implemented in the MVP; reserving them here keeps modality growth a data change. USER_NARRATIVE = the user describing an interaction in their own words (relevant to reported-speech handling).

source_channel.description: The communication channel, keyed to a dimensions-v1.json CH-* term where known. UNKNOWN is allowed and is not treated as benign.

content.description: The textual payload and its normalisation. raw_text may be absent for a URL-only or attachment-only submission.

raw_text.description: The submission exactly as received, before normalisation. May be redacted in place — see privacy.redaction.

normalized_text.description: Unicode-normalised, whitespace-collapsed, case-preserved text used as the offset frame for observation spans. Normalisation is lossless-locating: offsets into normalized_text must remain valid.

language.description: Detected/declared BCP-47-ish language tags (ISO 639). MVP knowledge is en only, but an envelope MAY carry any language; the rule layer flags unsupported input (rule schema on_unsupported_input) — the envelope never silently downgrades.

script.description: ISO 15924 script codes, e.g. Latn, Deva, Taml. Carried even when language is en so that a transliterated message (e.g. hi-Latn) is representable rather than mislabelled.

language_detection.description: How language/script were determined and with what confidence. Confidence here is EXTRACTION confidence, never a risk score (CONF-001).

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 instant the artefact was sent/observed, where known. Absence is UNKNOWN, not 'now'.

actor.description: The sender/originator, where any of it is known. Every field optional; data minimisation applies.

recipient.description: The recipient/target, where known. Typically the submitting user.

extracted_primitives.description: Structural artefacts a PARSER/SYSTEM_METADATA extractor can lift without interpretation. These are FACTS about the message, not indicators. Interpretation happens in the observation layer. All arrays default to empty; empty means 'none found', UNKNOWN is expressed by omission.

urls.description: URL facts, each conforming to url-observation.schema.json. Reputation/allowlist default to NOT_EVALUATED — never assumed malicious.

payment_handles.description: Bank/wallet/merchant handles other than UPI VPAs.

amounts.description: Monetary amounts with currency where determinable. Direction of any amount is NOT decided here — it belongs to the observation's payment_direction (WP2 STEP 8).

codes.description: Numeric codes present in the text (OTP-shaped strings, USSD/short codes, linking codes). Whether a code is being REQUESTED or DELIVERED is an observation-layer decision, not a primitive.

attachments.description: Metadata about attachments (images, PDFs, QR images). Content is not inlined; a VISION/OCR extractor produces derived text as a separate envelope or as observations. No attachment bytes are stored here.

media_type.description: IANA media type, e.g. image/png, application/pdf.

derived_text_input_id.description: The input_id of the OCR/VISION-derived envelope, if one was produced. Keeps the provenance chain traceable.

thread.description: Conversation/thread context where available. A single message is the common case; a thread lets stage-sequence signals (RESEARCH-003 §2) become expressible later without a schema change.

position.description: Index of this message within the thread.

prior_input_ids.description: input_ids of preceding messages, for cross-message reasoning in a later phase. Not required.

user_supplied_context.description: What the user tells us about the artefact. Critical for reported-speech: a user pasting a scam they RECEIVED versus one they are being asked to act on. Never treated as ground truth about maliciousness.

relationship_to_content.description: Feeds the observation attribution model (FIRST_PARTY vs REPORTED).

note.description: Free-text user note. May be redacted.

provenance.description: How this envelope came to exist. Distinct from the per-observation extractor provenance downstream.

received_via.description: TEST_FIXTURE marks synthetic data (G-09): a fixture-sourced envelope may never contribute to an accuracy claim.

pipeline_stage.description: An envelope is always at INGESTED; observation/indicator stages live in their own artefacts. Const to stop the envelope being reused as a detection carrier.

normalizer.description: The normalisation tool/version that produced normalized_text.

synthetic.description: True for authored test data. Redundant with received_via=TEST_FIXTURE but explicit for downstream guards.

privacy.description: Data-minimisation and redaction metadata (NFR privacy, DPDP posture; retention/legal basis is OI-05, out of WP2 scope). Records WHAT was minimised so the decision is auditable, without storing the removed value.

redaction.description: Redactions applied to raw_text/notes before storage. Each records the class and span that was removed, not the value.

minimization_profile.description: Named minimisation policy applied (e.g. 'default-mvp'). The policy content is defined outside WP2.

span.description: Half-open character offsets [start, end) into content.normalized_text.

value.description: A dimensions-v1.json channel term, or UNKNOWN.

party.description: A communicating party. All fields optional; populate only what is needed and permitted.

handle.description: Phone/username/email/VPA as presented. May be redacted.

claimed_identity.description: Who the party CLAIMS to be, verbatim-ish (e.g. 'CBI officer'). This is a claim, never a verified fact; it feeds IDENTITY_ASSERTION observations.

is_known_contact.description: Whether the recipient recognises the party. UNKNOWN by default; never assumed known.

primitive.description: A parsed structural artefact and where it sits in the text.

value.description: The parsed token as it appears (possibly masked).
Magnitude only. This is not a severity or risk number (CONF-001).

currency.description: ISO 4217 where determinable (e.g. INR); omitted if unknown.
